messages:
Mira Chen: quick sync — proposing we add a "usability window" signal into canary gating, not just perf/errs. short idea below, want feedback before i draft an RFC.

Jordan Patel: usability window? can you sketch what that looks like in practice?

Mira Chen: yeah — instead of only monitoring p50/p95 + error rate, we track a small set of real end-to-end user tasks run against canary for 10–30m, and compute an "availability" metric: fraction of queries with acceptable latency+semantic pass. if it dips, rollback.

Ekaterina Sokolova: +1. from ML side we should include a tiny reference evalset (100 queries) and a fast semantic similarity check (embedding cosine + heuristic) to catch quality regressions that perf metrics miss.

Sam Rivera: sharing a rollout snippet I've used for internal demos — very light weight:
```yaml
canary:
  duration: 20m
  initial_traffic: 5%
  step: 10%
  evaluation_window: 2m
  metrics:
    - name: latency.p90
      threshold: 1.5x
    - name: errors.rate
      threshold: 0.5%
    - name: usability.availability
      threshold: 98%
fallback:
  trigger: any_threshold_breach
  action: route_to: baseline-v3
  cache_flush: false
```

Liam O'Neill: curious about "cache_flush: false" — in practice not flushing can hide regressions because old prefixes hit cached KV. we need to reason about cache priming vs visibility.

Ekaterina Sokolova: agreed. propose we separate two controls: observation-mode (no priming, purely passively observe) vs priming-mode (pre-warm small fraction of keys). observation-mode gives cleaner signal but higher noise; priming-mode reduces noise at cost of masking cold-start regressions.

Jordan Patel: sounds reasonable. how do we keep rollout fast while running those eval queries? we can't block traffic for 20m on every canary.

Mira Chen: plan: run eval queries continuously during the canary window in parallel (no blocking). evaluation window is sliding 2m buckets that feed the gating decision. also allow a "fast-fail" immediate rollback condition if error rate spikes > X within 1m.

DevOps Bot: deploy-bot: Canary started: id=k-20260320-17, model=llama-13B-q8, initiated_by=@Mira Chen, traffic=5% -> 15m planned. (reaction :rocket:)

Sam Rivera: another open question — statistical test. frequentist t-tests/p-values are brittle with streaming short windows. we've been experimenting with Bayesian sequential testing (posterior probs) to make decisions earlier with control over false alarm rate. anyone tried that here?

Ekaterina Sokolova: yes we've got a lightweight bayes bandit lib in evals. it gives posterior probability that metric is worse than control by delta. threshold like P(worse)>0.95 triggers rollback. smoother than p-values for short windows.

Liam O'Neill: ops concern: fallback path must be explicit about model and capacity. if fallback routes to baseline but baseline is saturated, we cascade. rollout controller should check fallback capacity before switching.

Mira Chen: agreed. proposal: rollout controller queries capacity oracle before applying fallback. fallback has two modes: "instant-route" and "gradual-escrow" (drain canary traffic into reserved capacity until steady).

Jordan Patel: final thought — record every gating decision and stash diffs in a release artifact so product can audit why a canary failed (latency spike vs quality delta). helps triage.

Sam Rivera: +1. also include a tiny trace sample of request/response pairs (sanitized) for failed evals. saved to the canary bucket.

Mira Chen: thanks all — i'll draft RFC with: evaluation-window semantics, observation vs priming modes, bayesian gating thresholds, fallback capacity checks, and required audit artifacts. will post a draft in #eng-platform tomorrow.

DevOps Bot: deploy-bot: Canary id=k-20260320-17 progressed to 25% (no triggers).

Jordan Patel: nice, feel free to ping me on the RFC for the capacity oracle API shape.

Liam O'Neill: want to run a tabletop next week simulating cache vs priming fallout. count me in.

Ekaterina Sokolova: i'll add a small reference evalset and code to run the bayes checks in the evals repo.

Mira Chen: perfect — closing the thread for now. thanks everyone. (reaction :white_check_mark:)
